questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I knew that I wanted to go to a university with high standards, and that was the impression I got when reading about the department of marine biology on James Cook University. I was also motivated by the fact that the Great Barrier Reef was within such short distance, thus allowing for a more hands-on learning, where I knew that I could go diving and actually see the ecosystems that we would be learning about through lectures.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was extremely easy, as James Cook University makes sure that every student knows where to seek the information they need. I was very confused, but the instructions on where to meet up the first day were very clear, and from then on, the staff were so helpful and understanding.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was picked up in Townsville Airport by a shuttle bus arranged by the university, and that was very helpful. I just had to let them know when I would be arriving, and then they took us each to our destinations.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I believe that I was very lucky in finding housing, as I just went on a Facebook-group, "TOWNSVILLE ACCOMODATION", where a lot of people were posting about available rooms. I then took contact to a girl, and I then decided to pay the bond upfront to her, which I know was risky, but I was willing to do that to insure that I had a place to stay when I arrived.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
Living off campus has its perks, but definitely also some downsides. I was lucky that I bonded very well with the girl whose house I moved into, and that allowed me to go to places that not a lot of tourists would otherwise have known. But on the downside, the students living on college on dorms are very quick to bond, as there is a lot of events planned for them. As a student living off campus, I found that it was easy to join, but that still calls for some friendships being establishes, so that you are invited.
The aspect of making friends was then a little harder and I felt that I had to be even more outgoing than the people living on campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The housing on campus was quite expensive, and I was able to find cheaper accomodation off campus.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There was a lot of booths set up, and then there were a couple of staff members from Student Service ready to register our arrival. The whole day then focused on getting us the information we needed by presenting a slideshow that contained the most useful points.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Student Service was open from 9-17, and they would make sure that they had resolved my issue before moving on.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was able to succesfully attend all the four classes that I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
I was a bit stressed about how I was going to be able to have my classes fit together, because I did not understand the system when I was looking it at home. 
So my advice (which could have saved me a lot of worries) is just to have a lot of classes approved from KU, and then figuring out which subjects fit together with the help of the Student Service staff. This was way quicker and much easier then wasting time figuring it out from home.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The academic programme was extremely adverse and so interesting. The academic level was also very high.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
The four courses that I took were: Marine Conservation Biology, Coral Reef Ecology, Aquatic Animal Ecophysiology and Ecological and Conservation Genetics.
For the first three courses above, the level of the courses were high, but doable. I learned a lot from them, but I will say that it took a lot of Saturdays at the library to be able to do so. The workload is generally so much higher than at KU, so there is a lot of assignments and midterms compared to UCPH, and that is definitely an adjustment. 
For the last course, Ecological and Conservation Genetics, the level was absurd. The lectures were the same for both BA and MA (which were the case for all my subjects, actually) but this particular course had extremely high standards, and for the most part of the semester, I was afraid that I would fail the course. In addition to a lot of assignments, there was a difficult midterm- and final exam, but also a huge assignment that we as bachelor students were expected to write on the same level as master students.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching differs quite a lot. The lectures are much alike in teaching style, but the fact that we often had to do small assignements and hand them in, is very different to UCPH. At UCPH, it is expected of the students to take responsibility for our own learning, where at JCU, it seems like the teachers were looking over our work constantly, making sure that we understood the material every step of the way.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Marine Conservation Biology
Coral Reef Ecology
Aquatic Animal Ecophysiology
Ecological and Conservation Genetics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend Marine Conservation Biology, Coral Reef Ecology and Aquatic Animal Ecophysiology to future exchange students. 
Marine Conservation Biology builds a good overview, and the lectures were exciting and very current. Coral Reef Ecology was a nice subject to have, as it provided me with the knowledge of a lot of different corals, that I then could go snorkel or dive to see closer up.
My favorite subject was Aquatic Animal Ecophysiology. The teacher, Jan Strugnell, was the most caring and motivating teacher, and there was a lot of lab work, which I also learned a lot from.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The costs of living in Australia matches that of Denmark pretty well, so I was not too surprised with any costs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Coffee was quite cheap compared to Denmark, as there is a huge coffee culture in Australia. This was certainly a plus, as I went for coffee with friends a lot of times.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of social sports: volley, soccer, kayak and so on. There were many social activities, e.g. parties, climbing trips, trips to the beach.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Climbing. There is a Facebook group called "Rockclimbers Association of NQ (Townsville)" and they host a lot of trips to Mount Stewart. Even if you have never climbed before, you can still go and learn. It is cheap (200 DKK for three months membership, thus including trips), and it is an experience you do not want to miss.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Crystal Creek (1 hour by car), Jourama Falls (1 hour and 15 minutes by car), Castle Hill (just in the center of the town), Magnetic Island (20 minute ferry ride from the town center).

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer:
It was easy, as the locals all were extremely friendly and outgoing. I can't count the times I've been called "doll", or "love" by non-creepy strangers. The fact that I would come home from school with bats flying over my head and to a wallaby sitting on my front porch was something that I was always just in awe of, so for me that was not too hard to adjust to. 
I found it much easier to make friends with Australians than Danish people, as there is general culture of being open and hospitable.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: The parties were the best for socializing.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not find any cultural differences challening.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I particularly appreciated the opportunity to learn more about the indigenous people and their culture, as it is a big part of the Australian mentality.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be prepared for an academically challenging semester - but also extremely rewarding semester. 
To make the most social connections, I would recommend staying on campus for accommodation.
And lastly, I was warned about Townsville on the grounds of it being a town of much crime, but I at no point felt unsafe. I was aware of my behaviour at night, but I felt that I was scared more than I needed to be at the beginning, because people around me kept telling me to be aware.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: For some of the courses, the field trips would cost around 1500 DKK (and for some other courses more), which would need to be budgeted. I was not aware of this when I chose the subjects.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part was all the friendships that I made with people from all over the world. I especially grew close with my roomate, and I know that I will have a friend for life.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I got decompression sickness during a dive in Cairns, and being in the hospital far from home was definitely a challenge. I went to the hyperbaric chamber in Townsville for treatment, but with the support from friends, I was able to recover and be able to finish the semester.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: JCU is a lovely university, and I cherished my time there. The campus is overwhelmingly stunning, with a lot of money being put towards the science department, and a lot of great places for students to study.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
